chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Bakr and Muhammad ibn Abi Suhban, from Hafs, from Amr ibn Salim and Muhammad ibn Ziyad ibn Isa, from Harun ibn Kharija, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Count Sha'ban as twenty-nine days. If it is cloudy, then start the morning fasting. If it is clear and you looked for it but did not see anything, then start the morning not fasting.'

key_terms.شَعْبَان: Sha'ban: the eighth month of the Islamic lunar calendar, immediately preceding Ramadan
key_terms.صَائِم: fasting: one who is observing the sawm (fast)
key_terms.صَاحِيَة: clear (sky): unobstructed sky allowing moon sighting
key_terms.مُتَغَيِّمَة: cloudy/overcast: weather condition preventing moon sighting
key_terms.مُفْطِر: not fasting/breaking fast: one who does not observe the fast

ai.seo_question: When should one fast on the uncertain last day of Sha'ban according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) gives a practical ruling on determining the start of Ramadan by sighting the new moon of Sha'ban. If the twenty-ninth night of Sha'ban is cloudy (making moon-sighting impossible), one should fast the next day as a precaution; if the sky is clear but the new moon is not visible, there is no obligation to fast, meaning the month of Sha'ban has thirty days. This ruling reflects the classical Islamic principle of moon-sighting (ru'yat al-hilal) for calendar determination, which was of critical importance for the Shia community under the Abbasid caliphate who could not always rely on official announcements.

en.hubeali: Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Bakr and Muhammad Bin Abu Sohban, from Hafs, fromm Amro Bin Salim and Muhammad Bin Ziyad Bin Isa, from Haroun Bin Kharjat who said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Count Shaban as twenty-nine days. So if it was cloudy, so wake up in the morning Fasting, and if it was clear and you can look, but you cannot see anything (new moon), so wake up in the morning not Fasting’ (so 30 days of the Month of Shaban).
en.sarwar: 9. Ahmad ibn Muhammad has narrated from Bakr and Muhammad ibn abu Suhban from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtariy from ‘Umar (‘Amr) ibn Salim and Muhammad ibn Ziyad ibn ‘Isa from Harun ibn Kharijah who has said the following:

“Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘Count of the month of al-Sha‘ban twenty nine days; if it is cloudy then fast, but if it is clear and you looked but did not see anything, you can remain without fasting.’”
